Running builds finish and settle. |
| 8 | Public canary: a brand new account signs up on cyrus.my, accepts the terms, buys a small token pack (live mode, refund it in Stripe afterwards), builds one mod | `/admin/cyrus/live`, Users & tokens | the ledger shows grant, reserve, spend; Reconciliation clean | as step 7 |
| 9 | Optional: `cyrus_public_enabled=true` (marketing page indexable) and the status page (nginx snippet `deploy/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-status.conf.snippet`, `CYRUS_STATUS_PAGE=1`) | | `/status` shows operational | remove the include, reload nginx |

Kill switches that need no deploy (Flags tab): global build pause (`cyrus_builds_paused`), AI gateway kill
(`cyrus_ai_gw_kill`), mod networking off. Use the build pause first in any incident: it stops new spend and keeps
installs, downloads and the wallet working.

## 3. First 24 hours: who watches what

One person on point (the owner) with the Discord alert channel open. Suggested rhythm: every 15 min for the first
2 h, hourly until the first night, then at 06:00 and 18:00.

| Look at | Healthy | Act when |
|---|---|---|
| Admin Live feed + Builds | success rate above 80 %, wait under 2 min | failure rate alert, or 3 identical errors: incident "bad build shipped" / "AI backend down" |
| Cost tab | under `cyrus_cost_alert_platform_daily_usd`, per-build average near $0.30 | spend spike: incident "cost spike" |
| Users & tokens + Reconciliation | every spend has a ledger row, no negative balance | ledger alert: incident "token ledger discrepancy" |
| Discord alerts | silent | any CRITICAL: run the matching section below |
| Stripe dashboard (live) | webhooks 2xx | failures: incident "Stripe webhook failure" |
| `launch-check.sh public` at +1 h, +6 h, +24 h | GO | any new FAIL |
| Disk `/` (89 % on 2026-10-14) and `/tank` | under 80 % | clear logs/caches on `/` BEFORE launch; never a build on `/` |

## 4. Incident runbook

For every incident: note the time, post in the owner channel, set the build pause if money or customer data is at risk,
fix, write the cause in `docs/cyrus/07-operations.md` playbook table.

### AI backend down (`ai-backend-burst` alert, or builds fail with `ai_unavailable` / session limit)
1. Admin Builds: confirm the errorCode and that it is not one prompt. `curl localhost:7340/health` from the primary.
2. Pause builds (Flags > global build pause). Failures are free for customers (tokens released), but retries burn goodwill.
3. Key problem (auth errors, 401/403, billing): rotate or top up the API key in the Anthropic console, then
   `API_KEY=... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh`. Provider outage: wait, post to the status feed, resume.
4. Resume, canary one build, watch the failure-rate alert clear.

### Build backlog (`queue-depth` alert: more than `cyrus_alert_queue_depth` queued, or oldest over 15 min)
1. Builds tab: are builds running (service concurrency) or stuck? `health` shows `running` and `queued`.
2. Stuck at one stage: restart the build service container from VM 88001 (owner action), queued builds are re-picked.
3. Genuine load: leave the pause OFF only if wait stays under 10 min; otherwise pause and let it drain, tell users.
4. Check node-2 disk and the test-flight host if flights are the slow stage.

### Cost spike (`ai-spend-24h` critical)
1. Cost tab: by account, by prompt kind, repair share. One account: suspend or set `cyrus_cost_user_daily_cap_usd`.
2. Platform wide: lower `cyrus_cost_platform_daily_cap_usd` (new builds refused with 503 above it), or pause builds.
3. If repair share jumped, the last image or prompt change is suspect: run the eval gate, roll the image back
   (`TAG=<previous> bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh`).

### Bad build shipped (customer reports a crash / a mod breaks servers)
1. Find the build in admin Builds (engine release record, flight verdict). Check whether the flight gate ran.
2. Stop the spread: hide/take down the community page if published (Community tab), disable the mod on affected
   servers through the lifecycle tools; the delivery path rolls back exact bytes.
3. If the cause is the engine: pause builds, roll the image back, re-run the eval gate, then resume. Credit affected
   accounts through Users & tokens (comp/refund, audited).

### Token ledger discrepancy (`ledger-anomaly` critical)
1. Reconciliation tab names the accounts. The ledger is append-only and idempotent: the ledger is the truth, the
   balance is derived. Never edit rows by hand.
2. Pause builds if more than a handful of accounts differ (a settle bug). For one account use an audited admin
   grant/revoke to correct, never SQL.
3. Stale reservations (over 2 h) mean a settle job died: restart `nxeon-worker`; reservations release on retry.

### Stripe webhook failure (`webhook-failures`, or Stripe dashboard shows non-2xx)
1. Stripe dashboard: the response code and body. 400 = signing secret mismatch (live vs test secret, the usual cause
   after the live swap); 5xx = web down; timeout = primary overloaded.
2. Fix the secret in the portal env and promote/restart. Then resend the failed events from the Stripe dashboard; the
   handler is idempotent by session id.
3. Check Reconciliation for paid-but-ungranted tokens before closing.

### Data-subject request (access / export / erasure)
1. Verify identity through the account email, never a ticket claim alone. Owner sign-off before replying.
2. Export: the account data export (`/api/account/export`) plus Cyrus data (projects, ledger) from admin Users & tokens.
3. Erasure: admin GDPR erase (`CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE` on, typed confirmation). Check what it removes (`lib/cyrus/admin/ops.ts`)
   before replying: the token ledger is append-only by design, so say plainly what is kept for accounting. Backups
   age out under the retention in the backups section (14 daily, 8 weekly on node-2; 7/5/6 off-box), so state a
   90 day horizon.
4. Log the request and its completion in the audit tab.

## 5. On-call cheat sheet

```
scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh public           # GO / NO-GO with fixes (read only)
scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh service         # build service: auth, image, queue
scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh --dry-run          # every alert rule, nothing posted
curl -s localhost:7340/health | head -c 400     # build service raw
systemctl status nxeon-web nxeon-worker cyrus-alerts.timer
journalctl -u nxeon-web --since -15min | grep -i cyrus | tail
```

| Symptom | First move | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Studio won't load | `curl https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | `systemctl status nxeon-web`; `nginx -t`; Cloudflare status |
| Builds all fail | pause builds | AI backend down section |
| Builds slow | `health` queued/running | backlog section |
| Money looks wrong | pause builds | ledger section; never SQL |
| Customer reports crash | find build | bad build section |
| Disk alert | `df -h / /tank` | clear known caches on `/`; never build on `/` |
| Cert alert | `certbot certificates` | `certbot renew`; check Cloudflare edge cert |
| Backup stale | `cat /tank/cyrus-backups/LAST_SUCCESS` (node-2) | `systemctl status cyrus-backup`; run `backup-nightly.sh --go` |

Rules that still apply: never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon`; never `pkill -f`; never run role/ownership SQL; never
print `.env`; do not reply to support tickets without the owner's sign-off.
=========
# cyrus.my launch: host readiness (PREPARED, NOTHING APPLIED)

Status 2026-10-13, branch `feature/cyrus-portals`. This file only prepares the work: no nginx edit, env write, flag change, DNS, Cloudflare or Stripe change has been made. Every step below is for the owner (or a parent session with the owner's go) to run, in order, with the rollback beside it.

What exists today: the static landing (v7) is live on `cyrus.my` from `/var/www/cyrus.my` (nginx server block `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cyrus-my`: `/` and `/packs/p/<sha1>.zip` only, no proxy). The app already contains the whole dual-host layer (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, `lib/cyrus/bridge/*`, `middleware.ts`, `app/cyrus-host/*`); it is dormant because no request reaches the app on that hostname.

## 1. What the app does on cyrus.my (read from code)
Source: `lib/cyrus/bridge/config.ts`, `routing.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `app/cyrus-host/*`, tests `test/cyrus-bridge-routing.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-admin-host.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-portals-routing.test.ts`.

| Public path on cyrus.my | Result |
|---|---|
| `/` | nginx static landing. If it ever reaches the app: 302 `/studio` |
| `/studio[/...]` | rewritten to `/dashboard/cyrus[/...]` (the studio, Cyrus chrome) |
| `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/assets`, `/servers`, `/wallet`, `/projects[/<id>]` | customer app (`/dashboard/cyrus/app/*`), 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off |
| `/help[/<slug>]`, `/plans` | help center and plans page (read-only, 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off) |
| `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/auth/nxeon/start`, `/auth/nxeon/callback`, `/auth/handoff`, `/auth/logout` | Cyrus-host auth pages (`app/cyrus-host/*`, 404 on every other host) |
| `/api/cyrus/*`, `/api/mod-builder/*`, `/api/nxlabs/cyrus*` | the same handlers as on Nxeon |
| `/dashboard/<anything else>` | 302 to the same path on `APP_URL` (Nxeon) |
| `/login`, `/register` | 302 to `/sign-in`, `/sign-up` |
| `/mods/cyrus/*`, `/admin`, `/staff`, `/sso/*`, everything else | 404 |
| `/_next/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/.well-known/*`, `/vendor/*`, static file extensions | pass |

Gaps found while reading, and what to do about them:
1. **Community pages are not served on cyrus.my** (`/mods/cyrus` is a 404 there by design). The generated Featured mods section therefore links to `https://nxeon.cloud/mods/cyrus/<slug>` (`featured.mjs --origin`). If you want them on cyrus.my, that is a routing change plus a test, not a config change.
2. **`/api/cyrus/featured` passes** (prefix `/api/cyrus`). The landing generator reads it at build time. The landing page itself also calls `GET /api/cyrus/launch` (same prefix, anonymous) for the launch state and real plan numbers; both degrade to static private-beta wording.
3. nginx must forward only the paths the app serves (section 3) and keep everything else static, otherwise a scanner hits the app for every random path. The app 404s them anyway, so this is load, not safety.
4. The app trusts `X-Real-IP` and the LAST `X-Forwarded-For` hop; with Cloudflare in front, nginx must restore the real visitor IP (`deploy/cloudflare`, already built) or rate limits see Cloudflare's addresses.
5. No WebSocket path is exposed on cyrus.my (the Nxeon terminal and console sockets stay on nxeon.cloud). The `Upgrade` headers in the block below are copied from the Nxeon block and are harmless.

## 2. Environment (names only; set in the app's env file on the primary, then restart `nxeon-web`)
| Variable | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` | `1` | master switch; unset = nothing changes for any request |
| `CYRUS_HOSTS` | `cyrus.my,www.cyrus.my` (default) | exact hostnames that get Cyrus chrome; first entry is the apex |
| `CYRUS_ORIGIN` | `https://cyrus.my` (default) | callback and return base |
| `APP_URL` | `https://nxeon.cloud` (already set) | the Nxeon origin: identity provider, wallet, `/dashboard/*` hand-over |
| `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` | `1` | customer app + help center + plans (also needs the studio gate) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST` | `<16-63 [a-z0-9]>.cyrus.my` | secret admin host (kept ONLY in env and the password manager) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS` | optional exact staff IPs | other IPs get 404 (reads `X-Real-IP`) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY` | `1` only after the admin host works | `/admin/cyrus` 404s on every other host |
| `CYRUS_BRIDGE_REQUIRE_VERIFIED` | leave default (strict) | Cyrus sign-in needs a verified email |
| `CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN` + `CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` + `CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | `1` + the "Cyrus oAuth" client | optional "Continue with Google" on cyrus.my; default off; runbook [CYRUS-GOOGLE-LOGIN](CYRUS-GOOGLE-LOGIN.md) (needs `api/auth/google` in the nginx regex below) |
| `CYRUS_WALLET_PAY` | `1` if wallet top-ups should work from cyrus.my | optional |
| `ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_API_KEY` | optional | Economy tab live Anthropic costs (server only; not needed for launch) |

Session and SSO: no setting to change. The Cyrus session cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` (Secure, path `/`, no Domain, so it cannot be shared with or set from another host); SSO state cookies are `__Host-*_sso_state`; the callback URLs are the exact strings `https://cyrus.my/auth/nxeon/callback` and `https://nxeon.cloud/sso/cyrus/return`. Signing keys are derived from `AUTH_SECRET` unless the `CYRUS_BRIDGE_*_KEY` PEMs are set. Because cookies are host-only, signing in on cyrus.my never signs the visitor in on nxeon.cloud except through the consented SSO hop.

Also keep the pre-launch pair consistent (`cyrus_studio_public_enabled` and `cyrus_tok_live`, the smoke script checks it) and `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` for the community and featured API.

## 3. nginx additions (EXACT; add to the existing HTTPS block of `cyrus-my`, nothing else touched)
The static pieces stay: `location = /`, `/packs/`, and `location /` with `try_files`. Add one named location and proxy locations for the app paths. `nxeon_web` is the upstream already defined in `conf.d/nxeon-web-upstream.conf` and used by `nxeon-cloud`.

```nginx
# --- inside the existing `server { listen 443 ssl; server_name cyrus.my www.cyrus.my; ... }` ---
    client_max_body_size 20m;                 # attachments / images in the studio (same order as nxeon-cloud)
    error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;
    location = /maintenance.html { root /opt/nxeon/public; internal; }

    # app paths: proxied to the SAME backend as nxeon.cloud
    location ~ ^/(studio|home|new|account|assets|servers|wallet|projects|help|plans|sign-in|sign-up|auth|login|register|dashboard|legal|api/auth/google|api/cyrus|api/mod-builder|api/nxlabs/cyrus|_next|vendor)(/|$) {
        proxy_pass http://nxeon_web;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_read_timeout 600s;              # builds stream for minutes
        proxy_send_timeout 600s;
        proxy_buffering off;                  # live build streams (SSE) must not be buffered
    }
    # the favicon and the app's well-known files come from the app, not the static root
    location = /favicon.ico { proxy_pass http://nxeon_web; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; }
```
Notes:
- The landing's own assets live under `/assets/` and `/fonts`-style paths inside the static root; none of them collide with the regexp (`_next` and `vendor` are app-only).
- `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` stays on the HTTP block (certbot). Do not proxy `/.well-known/` on 443.
- Rate limits: reuse the zones the Nxeon block uses for `/login`: add `limit_req zone=nxeon_auth burst=15 nodelay;` inside a separate `location ~ ^/(sign-in|sign-up|auth|login|register)(/|$)` copy of the block above (the zone is defined in `conf.d/nxeon-security.conf`).
- Validate before reload: `nginx -t`; reload with `systemctl reload nginx` (no restart).
- A staging check without DNS: `curl -sk --resolve cyrus.my:443:<origin IP> https://cyrus.my/studio -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'`.

## 4. Cloudflare (zone `cyrus.my`)
1. SSL/TLS mode **Full (strict)** (the origin has a real Let's Encrypt certificate; the temporary self-signed one must be gone first: `openssl s_client -connect <primary public IP>:443 -servername cyrus.my | openssl x509 -noout -issuer`).
2. Always Use HTTPS on; minimum TLS 1.2; HSTS only after one week of clean traffic.
3. Real visitor IP: install `deploy/cloudflare/nginx` (CF-Connecting-IP -> `real_ip`) and the `cf-ips-update` timer BEFORE the app paths are proxied. Verify with the simulation test `test/cloudflare-realip.test.ts` and a request to `/api/cyrus/health`.
4. Cache rules (start from `deploy/cloudflare/cache-rules.json`; the list below is what this launch needs): cache `/assets/*`, `/_next/static/*`, `/packs/p/*` (immutable); **bypass** `/api/*`, `/auth/*`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/studio*`, `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/assets`, `/servers`, `/wallet`, `/projects*`, `/help*`, `/plans` and any request with the `__Host-cyrus_session` cookie. Never cache HTML of the app paths.
5. WAF: managed ruleset on; a rate-limiting rule of about 20 requests/min per IP on `/auth/*` and `/sign-in`; leave bot fight mode off for `/api/*` (the build stream and the API clients are not browsers). Do not enable "Rocket Loader" or "Email Obfuscation" (they rewrite the app's HTML).
6. WebSockets: not used on these paths. Live build streams are plain HTTP; Cloudflare closes a connection idle for about 100 s, so UNVERIFIED: confirm during the smoke that a long build's live view keeps updating (the studio polls and reconnects).
7. The secret admin host: its own proxied A record + Origin CA certificate (`deploy/cyrus/CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md`); never a per-host Let's Encrypt certificate.

## 5. Stripe (same account as Nxeon)
- Checkouts opened on cyrus.my are embedded Stripe Checkout sessions whose `return_url` is `https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/tokens/return?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` (storage add-on: `/api/cyrus/storage/return?...`), built from `returnBase`. Embedded checkout needs no return-URL allowlist.
- Dashboard: register `cyrus.my` (and `www.cyrus.my`) under Settings > Payment method domains (Apple Pay / Google Pay), same account.
- Webhook endpoint stays ONE (`https://nxeon.cloud/api/stripe/webhook`); fulfilment is idempotent and does not depend on the host. No new endpoint, no new secret.
- Customer portal / billing deep links open on nxeon.cloud (`/dashboard/*` hand-over). Plan prices in the Economy tab are display values; the charge is the Stripe Price.
- Test in test mode first: a card checkout, the return page, the token credit, then the same with the wallet (`CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`).

## 6. Order of work (each step reversible; stop at the first failure)
1. Land the branch; deploy with every Cyrus switch as today (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` unset). Nothing changes.
2. Cloudflare real-IP + SSL Full (strict) + cert check (section 4.1, 4.3).
3. Set env (section 2) but keep `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` unset; restart `nxeon-web`.
4. nginx: add section 3 to a copy, `nginx -t`, reload.
5. Smoke (section 7). Then `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP=1`, smoke again.
6. Admin host (separate runbook), then `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` last.
7. Publish the updated landing with `CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON` only when `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` is on and mods are featured.

## 7. Smoke tests (read-only)
```
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh flags     # launch pair consistent, switch combinations, env names (values hidden)
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh service   # build service reachable, auth api_key before any public launch
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh worker    # nxeon-web / nxeon-worker active, no recent cyrus errors
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh migrations
```
Plus HTTP checks (from outside, through Cloudflare):
| Request | Expect |
|---|---|
| `GET https://cyrus.my/` | 200, the static landing (same `ETag` as before) |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/packs/p/<known sha1>.zip` | 200 `application/zip`, immutable |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/studio` (signed out) | 302 to `/sign-in...` |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | 200 |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | 200 JSON |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/admin`, `/staff`, `/mods/cyrus`, `/random` | 404 |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/dashboard/servers` | 302 to `https://nxeon.cloud/dashboard/servers` |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/home` | 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off, 200 or sign-in redirect after |
| `curl -I https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | no `Set-Cookie` without a sign-in; later cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` |
| Sign in with Nxeon end to end | lands on `/studio`; Nxeon cookie NOT set on cyrus.my |
| `GET https://<admin-host>/` | 302 `/admin/cyrus` (staff only) |

## 8. Rollback
- nginx: restore the saved copy of `cyrus-my` (`cp cyrus-my.bak cyrus-my && nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`). The landing and packs are untouched by the additions, so rollback is instant and static-only again.
- App: unset `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` (and `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP`), restart `nxeon-web`: the app answers as if cyrus.my did not exist. Nxeon is unaffected throughout (separate cookie, separate hostname).
- Landing: `apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh rollback` (atomic symlink back to the previous release).
- Cloudflare: revert the cache and WAF rules you added; keep SSL Full (strict). Switching records to DNS-only exposes the origin IP and is a last resort.
- Data: nothing here writes or migrates data; the only new setting key is `cyrus_featured_pages`, `cyrus_econ_*` (projection inputs) and these can stay.

Inside the Nxeon portal panels (B.3) the same consent is offered as a button "Turn on Cyrus" that runs this flow in the top window and returns. 221 **Connect Nxeon (Cyrus-only person)**: signed in on Cyrus -> Account > Connections > Connect Nxeon -> same OIDC flow with `prompt=consent` -> `decideSignIn(incoming, session)` returns `link` -> `CyrusIdentity(nxeon)` + `CyrusNxeonGrant`. 222 **Connect Cyrus from the Nxeon side**: a deep link to `https://cyrus.my/connect/nxeon?return=`: Cyrus asks the person to sign in to Cyrus (any method) and then runs the Connect Nxeon flow above; with an existing Nxeon session this is two clicks. One protocol serves both directions. 223 **Unlink**: Cyrus Account > Connections > Disconnect (rule R5: never the last sign-in method; never Nxeon while a Nxeon-funded entitlement is active). Effect: Cyrus deletes `CyrusIdentity(nxeon)` + refresh token and calls Nxeon `revocation_endpoint`; Nxeon revokes `OAuthGrant` and every per-server grant (the r38 "rollback-only window after revoke" stays). From the Nxeon side: Settings > Connected apps > Cyrus > Remove = the same, via the `grant.revoked` event (`lib/nxeon-platform/events.ts` already has it). 224 225 ### A.5 Merge and conflict cases (implemented as a decision table in the prototype, 14 tests pass) 226 227 | Case | Rule | Outcome | 228 |---|---|---| 229 | Nxeon identity already linked | R1 | Signs in to that account only, even if the email changed | 230 | Same email on both sides, not linked (e.g. Cyrus-only via Google, later Sign in with Nxeon) | **R2: an email match never links or signs in by itself** | "You already have a Cyrus account with this email. Sign in to it (Google) to connect Nxeon." After that proof: link. No silent merge, no second account with the same email | 231 | Nxeon email verified only by the grandfathered / fail-open rule | R3 | Treated as unverified: never used for matching; sign-in refused with "verify your email on Nxeon first" (today's bridge already refuses unverified) | 232 | Signed in as A, the Nxeon account is linked to B | R4 | Refused (`identity_linked_elsewhere`), with "sign in as the other account" | 233 | Two Cyrus accounts belong to one person and they want one | Staff-assisted merge only (admin tool, audited): move projects/ledger rows from the donor to the survivor in one transaction, donor -> `deleted`. Never self-serve (token balances and plans make it a money operation) | | 234 | One side deleted | R7 | Nxeon account deleted -> `account.deleted` event -> Cyrus unlinks; if Nxeon was the only method: `pending_erasure` with a 30-day recovery window (email magic link to set a password), then `gdprErase` | 235 | Email change on Nxeon | sync rule | Cyrus updates its own contact email at the next Sign in with Nxeon when `emailSync` is on and the new email is strongly verified; the old address gets a notice. Nxeon also sends `account.updated {sub, fields:["email"]}` (no value); Cyrus re-reads `userinfo` with its refresh token, so dormant accounts stay reachable | 236 | Email change on Cyrus | Cyrus-only, verification mail; `emailSync` turns off | 237 | Unverified email (Cyrus email+password sign-up) | Account exists, can browse, cannot build, pay, publish or link until verified | 238 | Staff Nxeon account | R6 | Never a customer session on Cyrus (as today: `staff` error); staff use the Cyrus admin (F.2) | 239 | Suspended / erasing account | R6 | No session; existing sessions revoked | 240 241 ### A.6 Sessions, logout, erasure, support, bans 242 243 - **Cookies per host, never shared**: nxeon.cloud `nxeon_session` (unchanged); cyrus.my `__Host-cyrus_session` (opaque random value, row in `CyrusSession`, 30 days sliding, SameSite=Lax); Cyrus admin host `__Host-cyrus_admin_session` (SameSite=Strict, 8 h absolute, separate key); OIDC state `__Host-cyrus_oidc_state`. Different registrable domains, so no parent-domain cookie is even possible. Signing keys: Cyrus gets its **own** secrets; `AUTH_SECRET` is never copied (the move runbook already says so). 244 - **Logout**: (1) Nxeon sign-out / "sign out everywhere" / password change -> OIDC back-channel logout POST to `https://cyrus.my/oidc/backchannel-logout` (outbox + retries, existing `lib/nxeon-platform/events.ts` dispatcher) -> Cyrus revokes sessions with that `sid` (or every session of `sub`). (2) Cyrus sign-out -> Cyrus session revoked, then RP-initiated logout at Nxeon's `end_session_endpoint` (keeps today's "single logout both ways"; the user sees "signed out of Cyrus and Nxeon"). (3) Safety net when a logout token is lost: a Cyrus session created from Nxeon re-validates by refreshing its token every 15 minutes; a refused refresh (revoked, suspended, deleted) ends the session. 245 - **GDPR erasure**: each company erases its own data and tells the other only what is needed. Nxeon deletion -> `account.deleted {sub}` -> Cyrus R7. Nxeon's deletion page asks "Also delete your Cyrus account?" (if linked); yes -> Nxeon sends `erasure.requested {sub}` and Cyrus runs `gdprErase` (`lib/cyrus/admin/gdpr.ts`, already fail-closed behind `CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE`, ON in prod). Cyrus erasure -> `account.erased {sub}` -> Nxeon revokes OAuthGrant + server grants and deletes Cyrus webhook receipts for that subject. Exports: Cyrus' export already states "Cyrus data only" (`gdprExport`). 246 - **Support impersonation**: never crosses companies. Nxeon admin impersonating a customer: Nxeon's Cyrus panels call the Cyrus API with the subject assertion carrying an actor claim `act: {sub: , org: "nxeon"}`; Cyrus answers **read-only** (writes 403 `read_only_actor`) and logs it; no Cyrus session is ever minted (today's rule). Cyrus staff use the existing read-only, audited, 30-minute **view-as** (r40) inside the Cyrus admin. 247 - **Abuse bans**: each side owns its bans. Signals are reason codes, never free text: Nxeon suspension -> `account.suspended {sub, reason}` -> Cyrus ends sessions; account-level Cyrus suspension only for `fraud|chargeback|malware|abuse`. Cyrus ban -> `account.flagged {sub, reason}` -> lands in a Nxeon admin queue for a human decision (replaces r40's direct "ban with optional Nxeon suspension", which writes Nxeon's `User.suspended` across the boundary). 248 249 ### A.7 Data minimisation: exactly what each side stores about the other 250 251 | Nxeon stores about a Cyrus user | Cyrus stores about a Nxeon customer | 252 |---|---| 253 | `OAuthGrant` (client cyrus, scopes, consent version, dates) | `CyrusIdentity(nxeon, sub, emailAtLink, linkedAt)` | 254 | per-server grants (r38) + their audit trail | `CyrusNxeonGrant` (scopes, encrypted refresh token, consent version) | 255 | hashed codes / refresh tokens | per-server facts for granted servers only (id, label, game, version, loader), refreshed, deleted on revoke | 256 | install records on its servers (`ServerMod`/`GameMod` with source `cyrus`, artifact ref + sha) | install job ids and results it requested | 257 | webhook receipts (idempotency, 30 days) | own contact email + display name (copied once, then Cyrus' own data) | 258 | wallet transactions for "pay with Nxeon balance" (reference `cwt:`) | for Nxeon-funded bundles: the entitlement grant ids | 259 | **Not**: Cyrus account id, prompts, projects, code, token balances, plan (fetched live for display) | **Not**: Nxeon billing, other servers, IPs, passwords, SSH keys, Nxeon session ids (only the hashed `sid` for logout) | 260

342	### C.1 Merchant of record
343	| Option | Segregation | Tax | Effort | Risk |
344	|---|---|---|---|---|
345	| (a) Nxeon stays merchant of record; Cyrus sells nothing (the coded default) | Weak: Cyrus revenue in Nxeon's books, Cyrus disputes on Nxeon's Stripe risk profile, Cyrus-only users must become Nxeon customers to pay | Nxeon's registrations | none | AI-output disputes/chargebacks hit Nxeon's account |
346	| **(b) A Cyrus company is merchant of record with its own Stripe account** (same Stripe *organisation* as Nxeon, separate account, descriptor `CYRUS.MY`) | Strong | Cyrus registers where needed; Stripe Tax on | M | Needs the entity first |
347	| (c) Paddle / Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record (they are the seller; Cyrus is their vendor) | Strong | **They** collect and remit worldwide VAT/GST/sales tax: attractive for a global consumer AI product with a young audience | M | ~5% + per-transaction fee; the Nxeon wallet cannot pay into it |
348	
349	**Recommendation (b)**, with (c) as the alternative your accountant should price: if Cyrus will sell to consumers in many countries, (c) removes most tax work. Interim until the entity exists: keep the current Nxeon account (the economy is off), but keep prices behind lookup keys and the Stripe client behind `host.billing` (already: `lib/cyrus/host/billing-own-stripe.ts` is the switch), so the cut is configuration plus a webhook route.
350	
351	### C.2 Wallet interplay
352	The Nxeon wallet is Nxeon's stored value (Nxeon's liability). Paying Cyrus from it means Nxeon pays Cyrus on the customer's behalf.
353	- **Recommendation**: keep "Pay with Nxeon balance" for **one-off token packs and storage add-ons only**, never for subscriptions. Mechanism: Cyrus creates a payment request -> the customer approves on a Nxeon page ("Pay $10.00 to Cyrus from your Nxeon balance") -> Nxeon debits (`lib/wallet.ts debitWallet`, reference `cwt:`/`cst:` as today) and records an intercompany payable -> signed `purchase.completed` webhook -> Cyrus credits tokens (`lib/cyrus/tokens/purchase.ts` already applies these envelopes idempotently by `idemKey`). Monthly intercompany statement: Nxeon pays Cyrus the month's wallet sales minus refunds.
354	- Refunds of wallet-paid packs: Cyrus requests (`purchase.refunded`), Nxeon credits the wallet, unspent tokens reversed once (`CYRUS_CHARGEBACK_REVERSAL` logic).
355	- Plans (subscriptions): card only, on Cyrus' Stripe. Saved Nxeon cards cannot be reused across Stripe accounts without Connect: accept one card entry per company.
356	- If the accountant prefers zero intercompany flows: drop wallet pay (the switch `CYRUS_WALLET_PAY` exists).
357	
358	### C.3 Invoices, refunds, tax
359	Cyrus' Stripe issues Cyrus invoices/receipts (entity name, address, tax ids); wallet-paid packs get a Cyrus receipt with payment method "Nxeon balance". Refund policy lives in the Cyrus Terms (`lib/legal/cyrus.ts`; owner questions 3-5 in the CT report). Stripe Tax with the Cyrus registrations; prices tax-exclusive or inclusive per market (decision with the accountant).
360	
361	### C.4 Free tokens with Nxeon purchases, bundles, game slots
362	- r41 grants tokens on Nxeon server purchases/renewals (computed in Cyrus from `server.purchased/renewed/refunded` events, `lib/cyrus/tokens/grants.ts`). Across two companies this is a **promotion paid by someone**. Recommendation: Nxeon buys them: `POST /v1/partner/token-grants {sub, tokens, reason, ref}` (idempotent by `ref`, lot source `partner:nxeon`, 90-day expiry as today), monthly statement of **consumed** partner tokens, invoiced to Nxeon at an agreed rate (unspent expired tokens cost nothing). Alternative: Cyrus pays as its own marketing.
363	- Bundles (a Nxeon plan that includes a Cyrus tier): `POST /v1/partner/entitlements {sub, tier, periodEnd, ref}`; the existing entitlement mirror (`lib/nxeon-platform/entitlements.ts`, fail closed) becomes exactly this "Nxeon-funded entitlement" channel. A funded entitlement blocks unlinking Nxeon (R5).
364	- **Entitlements' source of truth moves to Cyrus** (Cyrus sells its plans). Game slots and storage quotas are Cyrus settings (`cyrus_tok_plan_<tier>_games`, `cyrus_storage_quota_*`), unchanged; Nxeon reads them only for display via `GET /v1/account`.
365	
366	### C.5 What an existing user's tokens, ledger and plan become
367	- Ledger tables keep their rows and `userId` values (= the migrated Cyrus account id). Nothing is rewritten.
368	- Unspent **paid** lots sold by Nxeon before the cut: Nxeon's deferred revenue. At the cut, either Nxeon transfers that liability to Cyrus with a one-off intercompany payment, or Nxeon pays Cyrus as they are consumed. Owner's SQL to size it (read-only, run by you):
369	```sql
370	SELECT count(*) AS live_paid_plans FROM "CyrusPlan" WHERE livemode AND status IN ('active','trialing','past_due');
371	SELECT source, count(*) AS lots, sum(remaining) AS unspent_tokens FROM "CyrusTokenLot"
372	 WHERE remaining > 0 AND ("expiresAt" IS NULL OR "expiresAt" > now()) GROUP BY source;   -- paid sources: plan, topup
373	SELECT count(DISTINCT "userId") FROM "CyrusTokenAccount";
374	```
375	- Live subscriptions on Nxeon's Stripe (expected: none or the owner's tests): let each run to its period end, `cancel_at_period_end`, and offer the same tier on Cyrus' Stripe with the first period free (coupon). `handleCyrusStripeEvent` stays in `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` until the last legacy subscription ends, then goes.

# CT: Cyrus Terms of Service and Privacy Policy (2026-10-15)

Branch `feature/cyrus-legal` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-legal`, from `main` 89608a9f). NOT deployed, no flag, no migration.
Owner paste: portal promote only.

**These are DRAFTS written from the code and docs by an engineer, not by a lawyer. A lawyer must review both documents
before public launch. Nothing here is legal advice.**

## What was built
- `lib/legal/cyrus.ts`: the single content module (version 1.0, effective/updated "October 15, 2026", `CYRUS_TERMS_DOC`,
  `CYRUS_PRIVACY_DOC`, `cyrusTermsSections(email)`, `cyrusPrivacySections(email)`, `CYRUS_LEGAL_SITEMAP_PATHS`, `CYRUS_LEGAL.lastmod`).
- `components/cyrus/legal/CyrusLegalDoc.tsx`: renderer (inline `[label](href)` links, version/effective/"what changed" hook,
  metadata helper: title "Terms of Service — Cyrus" / "Privacy Policy — Cyrus", indexable, canonical https://cyrus.my/legal/...).
- cyrus.my: `app/cyrus-host/legal/{terms,privacy}` now render the Cyrus documents (AUP and SLA stay the Nxeon documents in the
  Cyrus frame; layout footer links all four). The middleware `/legal/*` rewrite is unchanged (test pins it).
- nxeon.cloud: the same documents at `/legal/cyrus-terms` and `/legal/cyrus-privacy` (`app/legal/cyrus-*`), canonical = the cyrus.my URL.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-legal.test.ts`. Docs: `docs/cyrus/06-portals.md` (new section), `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` change history.
- Contact email = the existing Nxeon `support_email` setting (default support@nxeon.cloud), read at render.

## What the pages say (15 bullets)
1. Operator is Nxeon; Cyrus runs on the one Nxeon account; the Nxeon Terms, AUP, SLA and Privacy Policy are linked (absolute nxeon.cloud URLs) and apply; Cyrus Terms win for Cyrus.
2. Cyrus is an AI-assisted Minecraft plugin/mod generator; output can be wrong; test before production; "as is", no warranty; Minecraft is a Mojang trademark, not affiliated, no Mojang assets provided.
3. No separate Cyrus password: sign in through the Nxeon account (Google offered on the Nxeon sign-in); 18+; private beta may limit access and change features.
4. Cyrus username (creator handle) and bio are public on pages/listings/credits.
5. Tokens: units tracking measured AI cost; no cash value, not transferable, expire (date shown in account); hold then settle at actual cost; our-side failures normally not charged (fair-use limit); refused/cancelled builds can be charged; a change request is a new build; no free-refine promise; daily limits.
6. Plans/top-ups/storage sold by Nxeon, cards via Stripe, no card number stored; renewals; downgrades/cancels at period end, no partial-period refunds; refunded/charged-back purchases reverse unspent tokens; refunds follow Nxeon terms and checkout.
7. Acceptable use: no malware/backdoors, credential stealers, griefing/takeover tools aimed at others, illegal or infringing content; we scan, review, refuse, remove, suspend; scans never called "safe".
8. Ownership: you own your input; rights in output to the extent we have them; output may resemble others' and may not be copyrightable; licence to Nxeon to host/run/scan/display; you are responsible for rights in uploads; game-derived content stays private to the job.
9. Publishing: private unless published; publishing grants a non-exclusive licence to host/display/distribute/fork/remix as the listing allows; Cyrus-authored assets may be added to a CC0 community library after filters, with no credit; takedowns.
10. Third-party AI processing disclosed (currently Anthropic), with a pointer to what is sent.
11. Availability not guaranteed; features/limits/prices can change; the Nxeon SLA does not cover build results.
12. Termination, survival, liability cap (three months of payments, from Nxeon Terms), indemnity, governing law = Nxeon Terms (jurisdiction where Nxeon is established).
13. Privacy: collected data = identity (Nxeon + Google), username, prompts/uploads, generated code/assets/logs/test results, token ledger and Stripe payment status, diagnostics/IP, support messages, cookies; purposes with legal bases; no sale, no ads.
14. Google user data section: openid/email/profile only; used solely to sign in and identify the account; not sold; no advertising; no transfer except to run the service/legal; retained while the account exists, deleted with it; user can revoke in Google; verbatim Google API Services User Data Policy / Limited Use sentence with link.
15. Processors and rights: Anthropic, Google, Stripe, Cloudflare, Nxeon infrastructure and backups, email provider; transfers; cookies/consent (180 days, 30 day attribution, reject as easy as accept); retention list; export and deletion in Account > Data (7 day export link, 14 day deletion wait, what is deleted/anonymised/retained); security; 18+; changes; contact.

## Claims and code evidence
| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Sign-in is Nxeon SSO, no Cyrus password | `app/cyrus-host/sign-in/SignInView.tsx` ("There is no Cyrus password") |
| Google scopes `openid email profile`, identity only | `lib/google-oauth.ts` `GOOGLE_OAUTH_SCOPES`; callback stores `sub`, email, name, picture (`app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts`) |
| Token = measured AI cost, minimum charge, multiplier | `lib/cyrus/tokens/economy.ts tokensForCost`, `config-pure.ts` (`cyrus_tok_min_spend`), docs/cyrus/05 |
| Hold then settle; append-only ledger; expiry | `lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts` header; lots expire |
| Our-side failure free, fair-use limit, refused/cancelled charged | `economy.ts settleCharge`, `INFRA_FAILURE_CODES`; `config-pure.ts` `cyrus_tok_charge_refused/cancelled`, `cyrus_tok_free_failures` (3 / 7 days) |
| Daily caps, lower for new accounts | `cyrus_tok_daily_spend_cap`, `cyrus_tok_new_account_*` |
| Refunds/chargebacks reverse unspent tokens | docs/cyrus/05 "refunds and chargebacks reverse unspent tokens once" |
| Downgrade/cancel at period end, no mid-period refund | docs/cyrus/05 storage add-on "never a mid-period refund" (stated generally for plans; plan code not re-read, see questions) |
| Stripe, no card number stored | docs/cyrus/05 Stripe; Nxeon privacy text |
| Scanning of generated/imported code | docs/cyrus/08-security.md |
| CC0-only library, game-derived never shared, BYO private | docs/cyrus/04-assets-and-library.md legal ledger and licence rules |
| Automatic contribution after filters, opaque contributor id | `lib/cyrus/library/backend/studio-hook.ts` (HMAC contributor id), flag `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE` |
| Creator handle public | `CyrusCreator.handle` (prisma schema), erased by GDPR table |
| Build service sends prompt/project to Claude, no network for the model | docs/cyrus/01-architecture.md data flow; 08-security.md |
| Learning data is outcomes only, no prompt/code | docs/cyrus/15-learning-loop.md |
| Consent 180 days, attribution 30 days, reject-all, ad ids need marketing consent, hashed email | `lib/cyrus/analytics/consent.ts`; CyrusConversion docs |
| Cookies: `__Host-cyrus_session`, `*_sso_state` | `lib/cyrus/bridge/config.ts` |
| Export (7 day link), deletion (14 day grace) | `lib/cyrus/app/data-jobs.ts EXPORT_TTL_DAYS/DELETE_GRACE_DAYS`; UI `components/cyrus/app/AccountPanels.tsx DataPanel` |
| What erase deletes / anonymises / retains | `lib/cyrus/admin/ops.ts CYRUS_GDPR_TABLES`, `lib/cyrus/admin/gdpr.ts gdprErase` (fail closed on `CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE`) |
| Backups age out (~90 day horizon) | docs/cyrus/LAUNCH-RUNBOOK.md data-subject request |
| 18+, liability cap, wallet, governing-law wording | `lib/legal/terms.ts` (Nxeon Terms) |

## QUESTIONS the owner must decide (I did not invent answers)
1. **Jurisdiction / governing law and venue.** The Nxeon Terms literally say "the jurisdiction in which we are established ... should be finalized with legal counsel". Cyrus Terms point to it. Needs a real clause (and the legal entity name and registered postal address, which appear nowhere in the codebase; GDPR and Google verification both like a postal address).
2. **Contact email.** Using `support_email` (support@nxeon.cloud). Want a dedicated privacy@ / legal@ / abuse@ address and a DPO/EU representative statement?
3. **Refund policy for Cyrus tokens and plans.** The text says refunds follow Nxeon terms and checkout, spent tokens are not refunded, and reversal on refunds/chargebacks. Decide: any money-back window for unused token top-ups, plan cancellation refund, and the stance on dissatisfied-with-AI-result.
4. **Token expiry numbers.** Text says "expiry date shown in your account" (config values: plan tokens 3 months, top-ups 12 months, server grants 90 days). State the numbers publicly?
5. **Failure charging.** Text promises only "normally not charged, fair-use limit"; settings could change the 0% partial charge. Confirm the public wording matches `cyrus_tok_failed_charge_pct=0`, `cyrus_tok_free_failures=3`.
6. **Retention periods.** Not stated by code for: server/security logs, support tickets, build records of non-erased accounts (kept indefinitely today?), project history after account closure, prompts at the AI provider. Decide and state numbers.
7. **Public mod licence.** Today: non-exclusive licence to Nxeon and users to view/download/fork/remix "as the listing allows", ownership kept. Decide whether published mods should carry a specific open licence (MIT/CC-BY/all-rights-reserved choice per mod).
8. **Community library grant.** Text says Cyrus-authored assets may be added under a CC0 dedication after filters. This is the "ToS licence grant (lawyer)" item in the tracker; confirm it is what you want, whether contributing is opt-out, and whether the flag `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE` is to be on at launch (the text is written conditional on it being on).
9. **Anthropic terms.** Confirm the AI provider's data use terms (zero data retention / no training on API data) and whether to name them as "no training" in the policy; the text only says Anthropic processes data on our behalf.
10. **Cloudflare, email provider.** Cloudflare is listed as a processor (zone cyrus.my is planned in CYRUS-MY-LAUNCH.md, not yet live); name the email provider if desired.
11. **International transfers / data location.** Primary is OVH (region?), build host node-2 is Hetzner FSN1 (Germany). Text is generic; name regions and the transfer mechanism if EU/UK users are targeted.
12. **Age.** Used 18+ from Nxeon Terms. Decide if Cyrus should allow 13-17 with a guardian (Minecraft audience is young; this is a real product risk).
13. **Account deletion deletes Google data.** Assumes deleting the Nxeon account removes `googleId`, avatar; verify in the Nxeon account-delete flow.
14. **Google OAuth verification mechanics.** The OAuth client redirect URI is on nxeon.cloud (`/api/auth/google/callback`) and Cyrus signs in through it. In the Google console the privacy policy URL must be on an authorised domain: decide between https://cyrus.my/legal/privacy (add cyrus.my as an authorised domain and verify it) or https://nxeon.cloud/legal/cyrus-privacy. Also the home page URL.
15. **Terms acceptance record** (below).

## Gaps found (not built, by design)
- **No legal acceptance versioning exists** in the platform (grep for termsVersion/acceptedTerms/LegalAcceptance found only offers/team/partner-invite acceptance, unrelated). Sign-in and sign-up only show "By continuing you agree to the Terms and the Privacy Policy" with links. I did not build a second system. To capture acceptance per version one needs a new field (for example `User.cyrusTermsVersion`/`cyrusTermsAcceptedAt`, or a row in the Cyrus consent snapshot `CyrusAttribution`), a migration (owner approval) and an interstitial at first Cyrus use. `CYRUS_LEGAL.version` is exported for that.

Integration: import `CYRUS_LEGAL_SITEMAP_PATHS` and `CYRUS_LEGAL.lastmod` from `lib/legal/cyrus` and emit them with `https://cyrus.my` as the origin. The nxeon.cloud copies are deliberately NOT added to the Nxeon sitemap (canonical points to cyrus.my). The sign-in links and the landing already link /legal/terms and /legal/privacy.
- Privacy policy says "Request export"/"Request deletion" are under Account > Data: confirm the label of the page on cyrus.my once the customer app (`CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP`) is on; deletion actually runs only when `CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE=1` and the jobs worker is on.
- Statements about "Learning data" assume `CYRUS_LEARNING` behaviours stay outcome-only.
- Withdrawing consent without a new sign-in does not stop an already queued conversion (open item R49-4/consent in docs 08); the policy says consent can be withdrawn.
- Nxeon legal nav (nxeon.cloud /legal/*) does not list the Cyrus documents (adding to the shared `LegalDoc` nav would 404 on cyrus.my frame); link from the /cyrus and /mods/cyrus marketing pages is a follow-up.

# BZ: eval realism (2026-10-14)

Branch `feature/cyrus-eval-realism` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-eval-real`, from main f347f27a). Verified via devhost (tsc, eval + launch-check + planner suites). NOT promoted. No paid eval run; dry runs only.

## Why
One messy real prompt (goblin creature mod) found two bugs the eval could not see: (1) plugin.yml lacked `depend: BetterModel`, the plugin could not enable, but the eval's `boot` stage (server starts) passed because plugins_enabled was not required; (2) the portal could not save the result (engine.toolchain over 200 chars), the build stuck. The tidy corpus and the headline numbers overstated quality.

## 1. Metric honesty
- New pure module `lib/cyrus/eval/realpass.ts`: seven SEPARATE stages: compiled, scanned, server booted (Test Flight `boot`), plugin enabled (`plugins_enabled`), commands registered, assets delivered (each planned lane shipped), portal sync ok.
- REAL PASS = built AND plugin enabled in the Test Flight AND all planned lanes shipped AND portal sync not failing. Not flown = never a real pass (counted `unverified`). real pass@1 = real pass with 0 repairs.
- Portal sync is OFFLINE (`lib/cyrus/eval/sync-check.ts`): every returned texture/sound/creature/data pack/design goes through the same `checkReturned*` validators as `assets/sync.ts` (an asset the portal would drop = failure), and the engine record the sync would write goes through `validateEngineRecord`. Computed per succeeded build in `runPlan`, stored on the journal result as `real`. Not covered: a real portal submit (dedicated eval user, out of scope), DB/store failures.
- Surfaces: `eval-run` report.md + console line (REAL pass first, old numbers beside), `baseline.json` (same schema id `cyrus-eval-baseline-1`, optional `realMetrics`, `totals.realPass*`, `results[].realPass`), `eval-journal-stats` (stage table, per-lane real pass, `--compare` shows real pass delta), `eval-gate` (metrics `realPassPct`/`realPassAt1Pct`, `realRegressions` with the same limits; only compared when BOTH sides carry it, so the old accepted baseline never fails for a missing field), launch-check `eval` and `eval-run` rows (REAL pass, plugin enabled % of flown, "booted but did NOT enable", old numbers; WARN below `evalMinRealPassPct` 75 PLACEHOLDER).
- Gap closed: the eval never requested the creature lane (`assets.creature`), which is exactly where the goblin bug lives. New eval lane `creature` (assetKinds `creature`), scored by `assetsStage` on `creatures` shipped.
- Docs: `docs/cyrus/07-operations.md` section "Eval realism".

## 2. Corpus
- `services/modbuilder/eval/real-world-v1.json`: 80 prompts (not in `loadEvalSet`, so the gate subset and python harness stay comparable; loaded by `loadRealWorld`). Strata: creature 24 (30%), GUI/economy/quests 20 (25%), items 16 (20%), datapack/world 8 (10%), admin/utility/minigames 12 (15%). Styles: short vague 23, specific 22, run-on 14, typos 10, chaotic 7, wrong-genre 4. Style from the owner's real ModBuild prompts (prompt text only) and `qa-owner-batch-prompts.json`; 12 prompts reuse the owner batch ideas or the owner's real wording, none duplicates the batch keys (all `rw-` prefixed).
- Every prompt: `expectLanes`, `expectOutcome` (build/limited), `mustHave {kind,value}`. Verifiable today by the Test Flight: enabled, command, datapack_loaded. Tagged but NOT yet verifiable: item_give, mob_summon, gui_open (needs an RCON check; honest in the file's `meta`).
- Presets in `scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts`: `--preset real-world` (80 builds, mid estimate $22.61, range $13.95-$31.26 on Saka, by stratum: creature $3.10-6.89, GUI $4.29-9.82, items $4.36-9.58, datapack $0.89-1.96, admin $1.31-3.01) and `--preset real-world-smoke` (24 stratified 7/6/5/2/4). Dry run prints the stratum estimate. Always run with `--testflight`.

## 3. Failure taxonomy
`lib/cyrus/eval/taxonomy.ts`: one primary class per build that is not a real pass: timeout/limit, budget cap, false refusal, perf guard, compile, safety scan, plugin missing depend, plugin not enabled (other), design none, texture check, asset check, sync/engine record, commands not registered, not flown, other. Printed ranked by `eval-journal-stats` and in report.md. Infra results stay out of rates but appear in the table.

## Measured on existing journals (no spend, re-scored offline)
- fifth1 (24 builds): old pass@1 100%, final 100%; REAL pass 79.2% (19/24). The 5 misses are asset-lane not delivered: 4 designer prompts downgraded to a plain build (cov-warps, cov-playtime-rewards, cov-tablist, cov-bossbar-titles; rc11 `designStrict` auto = downgrade, by design, but the planned design lane did NOT ship) and 1 texture check (ast-hud-icons). Plugin enabled 24/24 flown. Portal sync not_run (journal predates it).
- fourth1: old pass@1 76.7%, REAL pass 97.8%, real pass@1 74.4% (same builds, honest stages).
- Takeaway: the old headline hides the design-downgrade policy; owner decision whether a deliberate downgrade counts as "delivered" (today it does not: honest, and `full` pass already said the same).

## Tests
`test/cyrus-eval-realism.test.ts` (new, 22 tests: goblin shape not a real pass, not-flown unverified, sync validators, taxonomy classes + ranking, old-journal derivation, gate compatibility, corpus proportions/smoke/creature lane/plan estimate, dry-run CLI, stats CLI). Existing eval, launch-check, planner, mc-coverage, asset-quality suites green (190/190 in the relevant set); one existing assertion in `cyrus-eval-run-lib.test.ts` updated for the new row text. tsc clean.

## Owner / next
- Eval runs now need `--testflight` to produce any real pass; the weekly gate should run with it.
- After the next completed run, re-accept the baseline so the real-regression check has a reference.
- When the build service is idle: `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts --tag rw1 --preset real-world-smoke --budget 12 --testflight` (24 builds, about $6-9) is the cheapest first measurement of messy prompts; then `real-world` (about $23).
- Next metric work: RCON checks for item_give / mob_summon / gui_open; `--through-portal` submit mode with a dedicated eval user.

# DB: Cyrus marketing roadmap, built from what Nxeon actually did (2026-10-15)

Status: RESEARCH and PLANNING only. No code, no DNS, no send, no post, nothing under /opt/nxeon edited. Production DB was read with SELECT-only aggregate queries (read-only transaction, no PII written here; partners and creators are counted, not named).

How to read this: every number is tagged. **(DB)** = measured from the Nxeon production DB on 2026-10-15, window 2026-07-23 to 2026-10-15 (about 12 weeks; the site is young). **(note)** = from an agent note or docs file. **(web)** = from a fetched or searched page with the URL given. **(proposal)** = my suggestion with no benchmark behind it. **UNKNOWN** = nothing I read answers it. Where a vendor makes a claim about itself I say so; those are marketing, not evidence.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. The five things to take away

1. **Nxeon never had a traffic-quality problem it could see, then a conversion problem it could not fix.** Raw sessions in the week of 2026-10-05 were 80,003, human sessions 1,141, human visitors 671, signups 85, deployed 28, paid 4 (DB, GrowthReport). About 98.6 percent of raw sessions were non-human. Until the bot classifier shipped (2026-10-01) every top-of-funnel number Nxeon looked at was inflated. Cyrus must measure human-only from day one.
2. **The one channel that worked was not planned: AI assistants.** ChatGPT is the first touch of 31.9 percent of human, non-mod entry visits (1,583 of 4,969, 90 days) and of 402 of 1,019 signups in the last 110 days (DB). It cites concrete, factual pages (free Minecraft, pricing, game hosting), not generic content. For Cyrus, "be the page ChatGPT cites for 'AI Minecraft plugin maker'" is the first-order SEO goal, ahead of Google rankings.
3. **Volume without a path to a paid action converts at about zero.** The free-intent landing pages produced 83 signups and 0 servers (friction report, 14 days); of 108 free Minecraft servers only 19 (17.6 percent) were ever woken, 4 (3.7 percent) reached multiplayer, and 2 owners paid (DB). Cyrus's equivalent is: a signup who never gets a mod installed on a server and joined by a player is not activated, however cheap the signup was.
4. **Scaled, templated pages hurt Nxeon.** ~65,000 near-templated mod pages went live in about a week and Google stopped crawling them within days (analysis note 2026-10-06; 28 search-referred visits across 64,853 mod pages in 30 days). Cyrus's community mod and library pages must be a quality-gated trickle, not a flood.
5. **Creators want money up front, not commission.** Of 49 creators who answered Nxeon's partner outreach, 26 said no to commission, 15 quoted flat rates between $100 and $5,000, others asked for CPM of $10 to $25 (note, creator-fixed-fee CSV). The 50 percent first-purchase discount plus 40 percent commission programme produced 290 clicks, 18 signups, 2 paying customers and $6.60 of accrued commission in its first 19 days (DB). A Cyrus creator programme must be a hybrid (seed, code, fixed fee for the few that matter), not rev-share alone.

Also load-bearing and easy to miss: **Cyrus has zero real external users today** (1 token account, 23 projects, 1 user, 26 mod pages of which 2 are public, no waitlist exists, the private beta allow-list has 2 emails; DB). Everything in sections 4 and 5 starts from absolute zero. And **the plan prices are placeholders ("to be announced")**, so no price-based message or paid-acquisition ROI can be computed yet.

### 4.3 Content calendar tie-in with the SEO plan

Follow CQ section 7 (use-cases 1 to 10, guides G1 to G5) but gate each page on a reproducible build. Add: (a) the dungeon and goblin case files as the two anchor pages; (b) a "what Cyrus cannot do" page (limits as a trust and GEO asset); (c) a monthly "what we got wrong" post; (d) the prompt library once there are 50 opt-in passing prompts. Cadence: about 2 pages a week, never a batch drop. Measure with CQ section 8 KPIs and the alert thresholds in CQ section 6.
### 4.6 Referral loop (tokens for invites, with safeguards)

Design: invite link per user from the post-install screen ("send this to the friend who will join") and from the mod page. Reward both sides in tokens when the invitee's first build passes Test Flight and is installed on a server. Safeguards: verified email only; reuse `starterEligibility` (blocks throwaway domains, normalises alias addresses and plus-tags); idempotency keys in the token ledger; monthly cap per referrer (proposal 10); reward tokens expire; refund or chargeback reverses; no cash value; block self-referral by same device or IP cluster; fraud review of any referrer above the cap. Honest expectation: Nxeon peer referral produced 1 referred signup in total, so do not forecast this loop; it exists to give the activated user a natural next action.

### 4.7 Email lifecycle (use the shared shell and tracking)

Build on shell v2 (header, dark card, icon tile, gradient button, footer, tracking pixel, rewritten links, one-click unsubscribe, secret-link exemption). Send via marketing class `product_news` only where it is promotion; transactional where it is account state. Event-triggered, never blast:

| # | Trigger | Message | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Waitlist join | Confirm, position, share link | Double opt-in |
| 2 | Invite | "Your invite", 3 starter prompts that prefill `/new?prompt=` | Reduces the blank-box problem |
| 3 | Signup, no build in 24h | One tailored starter (based on "what do you want to build") | Activation |
| 4 | Build finished | Result, cost, install button | Critical-path mail (highest engagement type on Nxeon) |
| 5 | Build failed or refunded | What happened, tokens returned, what to try | Trust |
| 6 | Passed but not installed (1h) | "Install on your server" or "download JAR + 3 steps" | Gap on the path |
| 7 | Installed, no player joined (24h) | Join address (Java and Bedrock if applicable), share card | Nxeon free-MC finding: "how do I invite a friend" was the first-hour question |
| 8 | First mod live | "Publish it" page and share image | Public page loop |
| 9 | Low tokens or daily cap hit | Plan options, honest cost | Revenue |
| 10 | Dormant 7, 21, 45 days | What's new + one suggested build | Retention (Nxeon: ~5% of signups return) |

Success metric per mail is the next product event, not opens (Nxeon: open rates 8 to 21% on drips; opens are unreliable). Frequency cap: one marketing mail per 3 days per user, none if they built in the last 24 hours. Note: `CYRUS_NOTIFY` must be set and the mail class mapped.

### 4.8 In-product growth loops (use what is built)

1. **Public mod page to remix**: author tag (username), stars, ratings, install button, remix tree; "Make this your own" opens `/new?like=<slug>`. All built; CyrusRemix, ratings, stars rows are 0 today.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.

I want to make Minecraft: The Infinite Dungeon, a roguelike mode that must work in my existing survival world without touching it. When a player types /dungeon start the plugin creates its own separate empty void world the first time, saves their overworld location, inventory and gamemode, and puts them in a simple generated stone room; /dungeon leave, /dungeon status and /dungeon abandon put everything back safely. There are 100 floors; a floor counter is saved per player and shown all the time in a HUD that reads 'Floor N / 100' with the room type. For now only two room types: a combat room (spawn a few mobs, door opens when they are dead) and a treasure room (a chest, then the door opens). Going through the door goes to the next floor. Put floor count and mob counts in config.yml. Keep it small and solid, more content comes later.
----

  4. WALLET PATH CORRECTNESS
  ====================================================================
  Mechanics (purchase.ts:84-124, nxeon.ts:47-71)
  - Order is debit first, then credit, in separate transactions (non-atomic saga), with a compensating refund: `wallet.charge` (conditional decrement via `debitWallet`, never negative; idempotent per reference by looking for an existing debit row) → `deliverPurchase` → on throw `wallet.refund` (idempotent per reference). A lost step is covered by `reconcileWalletTopups`. If the refund also fails: state "pending" and reconcile credits later.
  - Replay protection on the credit side is solid: idemKey = ref = `cwt:<user>:<key>` (UNIQUE ledger key); `creditTokens` is single-transaction under the account lock. A repeated request returns "credited" (line 99) without a second debit.
  - Existing tests (test/cyrus-bridge-purchase-db.test.ts): once-and-retried, insufficient funds, failed credit refunds, event path pending/redelivery, reconcile, refund. They are DB tests gated by env (skip unless devhost DB).
  
  Weaknesses
  - (4a) wallet.charge idempotency is find-then-insert inside one transaction on `WalletTransaction.description endsWith [ref:…]` with no UNIQUE constraint (the comment at nxeon.ts:50-52 admits this). Two simultaneous same-key requests from different processes could both debit. The in-process `locks` Set (purchase.ts:19,96) only protects one process. Also, the lock lives in the module instance of whichever bundle imports it; reconcile (called from page loads) may not see it. Single-process deployments are fine.
  - (4b) Replay after compensating refund: charge row (debit) remains after `<ref>:refund`; a later call with the same key hits `wallet.charge` → `{ok:true, replay:true}` (line 53) without debiting, and `payTopupWithWallet` does not inspect `replay`, so it credits tokens. Net: wallet refunded AND tokens credited. Needs a prior real credit failure plus a client that reuses the key (the UI generates a fresh key per click: TokensModal.tsx:94), so low likelihood, but it is a free-tokens path via the raw API.
  - (4c) `reconcileWalletTopups` has no minimum age (unlike storage reconcile's 10 minutes, addon.ts:211) and `locks.has` is its only guard against crediting a charge that a concurrent request is about to refund. Race (credit by reconcile, then pay request's own refund) gives tokens AND money; narrow.
  - (4d) `refundWalletTopup` (purchase.ts:172-187) revokes tokens first, then `wallet.refund`; if the wallet refund throws, tokens are gone and money is not returned, and a second call returns ok:false because the revoke is already counted (want - already <= 0). Also the single reference `<ref>:refund` makes any second partial refund a replay (money never paid). No caller exists, so currently unreachable except by tests.
  - (4e) `findByReference` is `take: 500 … orderBy createdAt asc` (nxeon.ts:76): a global reconcile with more than 500 `cwt:` moves in the window sees only the oldest 500 and may never reach newer ones. Wallet reconcile has no scheduled run (only per-user page loads and a manual admin op), 7-day window.
  - (4f) Storage wallet: `applyStorageEvent` creates the CyrusStorageCharge row (addon.ts:55) and then upserts the account (65) without a transaction; if the second step throws, the charge row exists so every later application returns `applied:false` and the add-on never lands (wallet debited; the in-request path refunds, but the renewal sweep/reconcile do not). `storageRenewalSweep` has no per-row try/catch (193-197), so one throwing row aborts the batch. `reconcileStorageCharges` is never scheduled (no caller outside tests).
